Stylized model distribution of identical copies

Source: R/utils_distributions.R
identical_model.Rd

Generate relevant quantities of a stylized model distribution for two identical copies of an ordinal measurement scale and a specified linear combination of items. In this stylized model distribution, items of the measurement scale have equal marginal response distributions and equal within-scale correlations.

identical_model(X = simple_scale(...), ...)

Arguments

X

list of relevant quantities for an ordinal measurement scale and a certain linear combination of items, as returned by [simple_scale()].

...

additional arguments by default to be passed to [simple_scale()].

Value

A list with the following components:

X, Y

each is a list with the following components detailing the distribution of the ordinal measurement scale:

  • `cat`: vector of response categories, encoded as `-M`, `-M+1`, ..., `M-1`, `M`.

  • `prob`: vector of response probabilites, shared by all items.

  • `K`: number of response categories.

  • `M`: upper bound of the support region of the items, with the lower bound given by `-M`.

  • `keys`: vector indicating whether items are positively keyed (`1`) or negatively keyed (`-1`). Its elements are simply derived as the signs of the weight vector of the linear combination.

  • `mean`: vector of means of the items.

  • `cov`: covariance matrix of the items.

cov_XY

cross-covariance matrix of the measurement scales.

a

weight vector for the linear combination `U` of items in the ordinal measurement scale from `X`.

b

weight vector for the linear combination `V` of items in the ordinal measurement scale from `Y`.

U, V

each is a list with the following components detailing the distribution of the linear combination of the ordinal measurement scale:

  • `M`: upper bound of the support region of the linear combination, with the lower bound given by `-M`.

  • `mean`: mean of the linear combination.

  • `var`: variance of the linear combination.

cov_UV

covariance between the linear combinations of the ordinal measurement scales.

rho

correlation between the linear combinations of the ordinal measurement scales.

Note

This is intended for maximum bias and breakdown value calculations relating to a stricter definition of the latter that is commonly found in the statistical literature. It defines the breakdown value as the smallest contamination fraction so that the correlation functional at the contaminated distribution is negative for two random variables with correlation 1 at the model distribution.

References

M. Welz, A. Archimbaud, A. Alfons (2026). Quantifying the impact of careless responding. PsyArXiv. doi:10.31234/osf.io/8fj6p_v2 .

See also

[max_bias()], [breakdown()]

Author

Andreas Alfons

Examples

model_XX <- identical_model(prob = "centered", K = 9,
                            length = 5, rho_w = 0.4)

# compute breakdown value
breakdown(model_XX)
#> [1] 0.09691076

# verification with maximum bias
max_bias(model_XX, epsilon = breakdown(model_XX))
#> $epsilon
#> [1] 0.09691076
#> 
#> $rho
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $rho_upward
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $bias_upward
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $rho_downward
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $bias_downward
#> [1] -1
#>
